revised_Text: The appendix easily becomes {{c1::obstructed}} and, as a result, inflamed and infected — appendicitis, one of the major causes of severe abdominal distress.
revised_Back_Extra:

Cue: the appendix opens into the cecum in the right lower quadrant, so its distress is felt low on the right side of the abdomen.

Confirmed leak, and it is worse than a single-blank leak — the visible apposition 'that is, behind the peritoneum' compromises TWO clozes at once. On the c2 card it spells out the hidden 'retroperitoneal space' (retro = behind, peritoneal = peritoneum), and on the c1 card the word 'behind' hands a non-knower the anterior/posterior forced choice. Structural finding: 'retroperitoneal space' and 'behind the peritoneum' CANNOT coexist in one note. Same cloze number gives R10/R10b's synonym-equation husk ('in the ___ — that is, ___', a synonym connective flanked by two same-number blanks); different numbers give the leak Parker flagged. The R3 two-way-definition carve-out does not rescue it either, because the 'meaning' side here is pure etymology rather than information — both directions decode without recall, so the pair carries no testable content. Correct resolution is to keep the two facts that a non-knower genuinely cannot decode (posterior wall, retroperitoneal space) in the Text and move the etymology to a Back Extra 'Meaning:' line, where it also gains the grounded detail from FIGURE 6-42's caption (behind the organs of the digestive system). If you want 'behind the peritoneum' actively tested, it needs its OWN note contrasting the retroperitoneal space with the peritoneal cavity — it cannot ride on the kidney card.
revised_Text: The kidneys lie on the {{c1::posterior::anterior or posterior}} muscular wall of the abdomen, in the {{c2::retroperitoneal space::body region}}.
revised_Back_Extra:
Meaning: retroperitoneal means behind the peritoneum, so the whole urinary system sits behind the organs of the digestive system.

Distinguish: the pancreas occupies that same space, which is why it is fixed deep in the abdomen and not easily damaged.
